Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for Bangladesh's second innings to commence. It will be Shadman Islam and Mahmudul Hasan Joy to open the innings for the home side. Victor Nyauchi will open the attack for Zimbabwe. Here we go!
... THIRD INNINGS ...

The Bangladesh openers have a job on their hands in these closing stages of the day, with the hard new ball posing a serious challenge. Ideally, the hosts will be hoping to get through to the close of play without any damage. Will they succeed in doing so? Let’s find out. Back in a bit with the reply.

Bangladesh started the day well, claiming four wickets in the first session, but couldn’t quite capitalise as the middle and lower order offered stiff resistance. Even the tail wagged longer than expected, and the visitors couldn't manage to keep the lead in check. Mehidy Hasan Miraz was the standout with the ball, finishing with a five-wicket haul, while Nahid Rana impressed early on with three wickets.

Zimbabwe end up with a lead of 82 runs! It didn’t seem likely they would stretch it this far when the 8th wicket fell with the lead at just 32. Credit to the tail for digging in and frustrating the hosts. That said, it could have been a much bigger advantage had the earlier batters capitalised on their starts. 5 of the top 7 reached double digits, but apart from Brian Bennett and Sean Williams, none managed to kick on and make a significant impact.

Madhevere fell to Khaled Ahmed, but Sean then formed a solid partnership with Nyasha Mayavo to take his side into the lead. However, a lapse in concentration led to his downfall. Mayavo was severe on anything loose and managed to see through to the end of the session alongside Wellington Masakadza. The assistance for the pacers was noticeably reduced compared to the first session, and with the sun peeking through, conditions became easier for the batters. Taijul Islam has been far from his best, and Bangladesh will be hoping for a stronger showing from him in the final session. For Zimbabwe, much now rests on this partnership to extend their advantage. Back in a bit for the start of the third session.

A good session for Zimbabwe! They've managed to edge into the lead, albeit a slender one for now. Sean Williams has grown in confidence as his innings progressed and holds the key for Zimbabwe in guiding them towards parity and potentially beyond. Bangladesh, however, will have their tails up, knowing that if they can dislodge Williams, they will be into an inexperienced lower order, giving them a real chance to seize full control. Do join us back at 6.40 am GMT for the start of the second session.

Brian Bennett looked solid during his fifty, displaying composure and sound technique, but a loose shot at a crucial moment led to his dismissal. Craig Ervine and Sean Williams then combined to steady the Zimbabwean innings, absorbing the pressure well. However, their partnership was cut short when Rana struck upon his return to the attack.

Bangladesh were much improved with their lines and lengths in the morning session compared to the opening day and managed to reap the rewards. Nahid Rana set the tone early with a probing spell, and Hasan Mahmud soon followed, dismantling the top order with sharp pace and movement in the first hour.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get underway here in Sylhet. It's an overcast morning, but crucially, the weather remains dry. The conditions are tailor-made for seam bowling, and Bangladesh's pacers will be eager to exploit the overhead assistance early on. Ben Curran and Brian Bennett make their way out to the middle. Nahid Rana will start the proceedings with the ball on Day 2. Here we go!

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof is down by the surface. He observes that the pitch looks much drier today. Mention that the seamers will be in play throughout, and as a batter, you are never truly in. He adds that for the Bangladeshi pacers, it’s about hunting in a pack and maintaining consistent pressure. Maharoof emphasises the importance of playing with a straight bat and trusting their defence, especially early on.

The head coach of Bangladesh, Phil Simmons, is in for a chat. Mentions that Bangladesh didn’t quite do the things they needed or wanted to on the opening day. He says that despite the disappointing start, it’s just the first day of the Test, and there’s still plenty of time to bounce back. Simmons says that the team’s preparation has been good, and the key now is to leave the previous day behind and move forward with intent. Feels that consistency with the ball will be crucial, as that’s where they let things slip.

Zimbabwe, on the other hand, will be delighted with their performance so far. It was a well-rounded bowling effort which saw them dismiss the hosts for just 191. Their opening pair then showed great discipline and application with the bat, negotiating the new ball effectively to finish the day unscathed. The visitors will look to build on that strong foundation as they aim to tighten their grip on this Test. Stick around as the first ball on Day 2 is not far away.

Day 1 was a tale of missed opportunities for Bangladesh. With the bat, several players got starts, but none managed to convert them into meaningful contributions. Then with the ball, despite favourable conditions for the seamers, the Bangladesh pacers couldn't quite exploit the assistance and apply sustained pressure. They will need to hit the reset button and focus on putting the previous day behind them.

Hello, one and all, and welcome to Day 2 of the opening Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium. The visitors find themselves in the ascendancy and couldn't have hoped for a better start to their tour. As for Bangladesh, very little went their way after winning the toss on the opening day, and they will be eager to bounce back and make early inroads to regain some control in this contest.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Bangladesh will need to recognise that, apart from Craig Ervine and Sean Williams, the rest of the Zimbabwean lineup lacks much experience. If they can capitalise on the early morning assistance and make early breakthroughs, they could claw their way back into the match and shift the momentum in their favour. For Zimbabwe, the focus will be on starting steadily and taking it session by session as they look to press their advantage. It’s all set up for an intriguing Day 2. See you then. Cheers!

In response, Brian Bennett and Ben Curran showed great application and composure to tackle the early challenge posed by the Bangladeshi pacers. While the hosts’ pace attack lacked consistency, the Zimbabwean openers capitalised on the loose deliveries they encountered. Bennett and Curran stood firm, even as the light began to fade towards the end of the day to cap off a solid opening day for Zimbabwe on this tour.

Earlier in the day, under overcast skies, Bangladesh opted to bat first in what was a brave call given the conditions. Zimbabwe’s new-ball bowlers didn’t make the most of the early movement, often bowling too short, but things changed quickly once Victor Nyauchi was introduced. Mominul Haque, dropped on 0, made the most of his chance and fought his way to a gritty fifty, but that was the only real highlight in Bangladesh’s innings. From a solid position at 98/2, the hosts collapsed dramatically, losing 8 wickets for just 93 runs to be bundled out for 191.

It's official - STUMPS on Day 1! Zimbabwe take the opening day honours in the Sylhet Test and will be mighty pleased with how things unfolded, especially after being asked to bowl first. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will have plenty to reflect on. They have only themselves to blame for not applying themselves better with the bat and for lacking consistency with the ball in the final session.
